what: Every crossing over the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway from the state line to Socastee, in waterway miles, with the clearance a boat has under it when it is closed. Read from NOAA U.S. Coast Pilot 4, Chapter 12 (edition dated 01 NOV 2026), paragraphs 155 to 174. Names: SCDOT historic bridge record (Little River), Horry County road centerlines that cross the county's waterway outline (Barefoot Resort Bridge Road; the fixed bridges), and the Coast Pilot itself (Socastee, US 501, Fantasy Harbour).

also.quote: In 1983, numerous rock ledges were reported abutting the deep portion of the waterway from Mile 347.0 to Mile 365.5. Extreme caution is advised when transiting the area.

also.what: where the waterway joins the inlet
also.quote: The waterway joins Little River at Calabash River, and extends northeastward from Little River just north of the waterway cutoff and southward to connect the waterway with Little River Inlet.

Once past the jetties, a marked channel leads northwestward for about 1.8 miles to a junction with the Intracoastal Waterway. ... Extreme caution is advised when entering and leaving the inlet. The mean range of tide at the inlet is about 5 feet.
The route of the waterway enters Waccamaw River at Enterprise Landing, Mile 375.2, and follows the river to Winyah Bay.
Depths in the approaches and alongside the piers at the marinas are reported to be about 3 feet.
The Federal project for the Intracoastal Waterway via Albemarle and Chesapeake Canal provides for a least depth of 12 feet from Norfolk, VA (ICW Mile 0.0), to Fort Pierce, FL (ICW Mile 965.6)

positions: Positions are for the map only: the centre of the county road line where it crosses the county water outline (Public/Streets layer 1 and parcelapp layer 21, roads-icw.json in RAW), matched to the Coast Pilot miles in order from north to south; Socastee from the NOAA station position. Not used as addresses.
